articles.headline: Mets remove interim manager tag, hire Andy Green to 3-year deal
articles.description: The Mets have removed the interim tag from manager Andy Green, hiring him to a three-year deal through the 2029 season, it was announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
The New York Mets have removed the interim tag from manager Andy Green, hiring him to a three-year deal through the 2029 season, the team announced Tuesday.

The Mets have performed well since Green took over as interim manager, with a record of 37-38, after Carlos Mendoza was fired at the end of June.

The worst-case scenario -- that the Mets would effectively roll over down the stretch -- did not occur, with young players such as Carson Benge and Nolan McLean continuing to develop under Green's watch.

"Andy has connected with and pushed our players to perform, despite the disappointment of the season," Mets owners Steve and Alex Cohen said in a statement. "Over the last several months he has brought discipline, accountability and positivity to the clubhouse, attributes we were seeking in our next manager."

Green, who served as vice president of player development prior to being named interim manager by Stearns, managed the San Diego Padres for nearly four seasons from 2016 to 2019, going 274-366.

Upon taking the managerial job, Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns said Green would move back to the front office after the season.

"When I accepted the interim role, I didn't anticipate it becoming permanent, but the more time I spent with our players and staff, the clearer it became that this is where my passion and experience could make the greatest impact," Green said in a statement.

ESPN's Buster Olney contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Hawks trade Hield, Nembhard to Hornets for Finney-Smith
articles.description: The Hawks are sending Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks are trading Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday.

The Hornets are expected to waive Nembhard as part of the trade, sources said. The Hawks create a $2.1 million trade exception and the Hornets likely create a $4.5 million trade exception with the deal, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

Hield landed in Atlanta in the trade that sent Kristaps Porzingis to the Golden State Warriors but appeared in just seven games for the Hawks last season; the sharpshooting guard is due around $9.5 million this season and has a player option for just over $10 million for 2027-28.

 

Finney-Smith was acquired by Charlotte in a trade with the Houston Rockets earlier in the offseason. The veteran wing missed the first two months of the season for Houston and has three years left on his $53 million contract, including a player option for 2028-29.

Nembhard, an undrafted rookie last season for Dallas, was acquired by the Hawks in a three-team trade that sent Zaccharie Risacher to the Mavericks and Luguentz Dort back to Atlanta from Oklahoma City.

Nembhard, 23, averaged 6.6 points and 5.3 assists in 19.5 minutes per game last season.

articles.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Walker, Shough on the rise while Maye, McConkey fall
articles.description: Need a quick free agent pickup -- or roster overhaul -- after Week 2? These rankings are designed to help.
articles.body:
Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize the players for their future potential and/or to gauge their value in trade. Eric's top 100 can be found below the positions in this column. 

Quarterback

Rankings changes: Wow. Serious injuries to the top two selections from the 2024 draft and a late 2025 first rounder are the story, as fantasy managers will miss the Bears' Caleb Williams (hamstring), Commanders' Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Giants' Jaxson Dart (knee) for an undetermined length of time. Each was among our top 10 QBs. Perhaps the mercurial Williams will return far sooner, so he remains in QB2 range in these rankings, but the risk of reinjury is high. Dart may be lost for the season. Backups Jameis Winston and Marcus Mariota enter the rankings, and they may be playing for months.

With three passers dropping in the rankings, nearly everyone else rises. The 49ers' Brock Purdy, Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes, Saints' Tyler Shough and Lions' Jared Goff are all in the top 10. The Panthers' Bryce Young rises into safer QB2 territory, with room for more. The Patriots' Drake Maye, last year's No. 2 QB scorer, remains in the top 10, but perhaps not for long after two disappointing outings totaling 17.84 points. The Rams' Matthew Stafford rebounds from Australia and is No. 11. It is quite amazing how quickly fantasy value changes in the NFL.

Running back

Rankings changes: Volume is king, and no running back earned more in Week 2 than the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III. Will he stay healthy? That was an offseason concern, but so far he looks awesome and he continues rising into the top 10. For those that want Walker at No. 1 ... c'mon, we are not there yet. Walker versus Bijan Robinson? It feels premature, though Robinson does drop a spot behind Jonathan Taylor to No. 3. Praise Walker, but if a Robinson investor offers him for Walker, do it.

Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is among big risers at running back, though we lack confirmation of solid volume moving ahead (same with the Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson). The Buccaneers' Bucky Irving and Panthers' Chuba Hubbard rise to RB2 status, as their reported timeshares appear to be rather one-sided. Aaron Jones Sr. is healthy and seeing volume. Don't forget about the Saints' Alvin Kamara and Seahawks' Zach Charbonnet, and watch for injury updates on the Eagles' Saquon Barkley.

Wide receiver

Rankings changes: Many star receivers delivered in Week 2, but the rankings movement at this position happened in the late-WR2 range, as the Panthers' Jalen Coker, Packers' Christian Watson, Broncos' Jaylen Waddle, Jaguars' Parker Washington and Browns' Denzel Boston continue to add value. Perhaps they catch some early underachievers like the Falcons' Drake London and Cowboys' George Pickens soon. They have already passed the Chargers' Ladd McConkey and Lions' Jameson Williams.

articles.headline: NBA trade tracker: Updates for every deal of the 2026 offseason
articles.description: We have the updates, including players and draft picks, for every NBA trade made this summer.
articles.body:
Major NBA moves have already gone down this offseason, none bigger than the late-night blockbuster that ended a year-long Giannis Antetokounmpo trade saga.

The Milwaukee Bucks finally dealt the two-time MVP to the Miami Heat for four players, four first-round picks and a pick swap. Antetokounmpo likely won't be the only superstar finding a new team this offseason, as former All-Stars such as Domantas Sabonis could also be on the move.

More action happened less than 24 hours before the draft. The Minnesota Timberwolves sent Julius Randle and the No. 28 pick to the Brooklyn Nets for the No. 33 pick. The Nets also sent Nic Claxton to the Chicago Bulls in the deal.

The draft saw several trades -- including pick No. 47, which changed hands several times -- and sent Isaiah Stewart on the move to Memphis, ending the Beef Stew era in Detroit. And the day after the draft saw LaMelo Ball get shipped from the Charlotte Hornets to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Kawhi Leonard, after six seasons with the LA Clippers, will return to the Toronto Raptors, the franchise he helped lead to an NBA championship in 2019.

With plenty more deals sure to come, here are the details of every trade that has happened this summer.

articles.headline: Fantasy baseball lineup advice for Wednesday: Connor Prielipp leads pitching streamers
articles.description: Everything you need to know to set your fantasy baseball lineups for Wednesday's MLB action.
articles.body:
Check out all of our starting pitcher rankings and other lineup selection tools here to help you make smart fantasy baseball lineup decisions. All fantasy advice is geared toward ESPN 10-team leagues with standard scoring.

Note: All information is accurate as of the time of publication. For updates, as well as any breaking news that might impact today's MLB slate, be sure to check out the latest fantasy baseball buzz. 

Other resources: RP depth chart | 2026 Rankings

ESPN's 2026 Player Rater | Betting notes for Wednesday

Pitchers to stream on Wednesday

Spoiler alert: This is not the ideal slate to make up points in pitching. Connor Prielipp leads the way after posting a 2.70 ERA and 0.94 WHIP over his last five outings with 24 strikeouts in 26 2/3 innings. The Minnesota Twins are on the road against the San Francisco Giants, so the right-hander will work in a pitcher-friendly park and face a depleted lineup missing Rafael Devers and Bryce Eldridge.

Walbert Urena hopes to end his rookie season on a roll when the Los Angeles Angels visit the Athletics. The 22-year-old righty has completed at least six frames over his last four outings, posting a 1.93 ERA and 0.86 WHIP with 28 punchouts to just three free passes over 28 frames. Sutter Health Park has been a nightmare for pitchers most of the season, but the temperatures should be in the high 70s and the Athletics' injury-riddled lineup has struggled at home for a month.

Hitters to stream on Wednesday

The Arizona Diamondbacks face the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Lars Nootbaar has been leading off for the Diamondbacks against right-handers, and the Rockies will send Mason Adams and his 5.09 ERA to the hill.

The Minnesota Twins are playing out the string, but Royce Lewis and Ryan Jeffers are hoping to end the season on a high note. The club is on the road against the San Francisco Giants, with lefty Cesar Perdomo getting the call. His 3.72 ERA is misleading, considering he's fanned only 12 while issuing seven walks and yielding three homers in just 19 1/3 innings.

Paul Goldschmidt should be leading off when the New York Yankees take on the lefty Steven Matz and the Tampa Bay Rays. Goldschmidt's role has fluctuated this season, but he's been productive with the platoon edge, batting .309/.404/.592 versus southpaws.

After three hitless games upon returning from a long absence, Konnor Griffin has a .283/.333/.396 line over his past dozen contests. He'll enjoy the platoon edge when the Pittsburgh Pirates host the St. Louis Cardinals and lefty Matthew Liberatore. Griffin's power stroke is lacking, but Liberatore has served up 27 long balls in only 149 1/3 innings.

articles.headline: Spurs-Pelicans games in Paris, Manchester sold out, NBA says
articles.description: The NBA announced on Tuesday that tickets are sold out for the 2027 NBA Paris and Manchester games set for January, featuring the San Antonio Spurs and the New Orleans Pelicans.
articles.body:
The NBA announced on Tuesday that tickets are sold out for the 2027 NBA Paris and Manchester games set for January, featuring the San Antonio Spurs and the New Orleans Pelicans.

According to the league, approximately one million fans registered interest in tickets, marking the highest level of demand recorded for NBA Games in Europe.

The Spurs and Pelicans will play regular season games at Accor Arena in Paris, France on Jan. 14, then face off again three days later at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England as part of the NBA's multiyear agreement to play regular-season outings in Europe.

Basketball ranks as the fastest-growing sport in Europe, according to the NBA, just behind soccer with more than 270 million fans across the continent. In fact, a record-71 Europeans made opening-night rosters last season in the NBA, and represent approximately 15% of the league, not to mention five of the last eight players to win MVP.
